items.title: Next Wednesday, July 29, Inspired by the incredible acoustic properties of the Enterprise South Nature Park bunkers, per...
items.content_text:
Next Wednesday, July 29, Inspired by the incredible acoustic properties of the Enterprise South Nature Park bunkers, percussionist Artist-in-Residence Jess Tsang presents “music for resonant spaces”, a site-specific live performance for bass drum, feedback, and objects, utilizing the natural resonance of the concrete structure as its own instrument.
 ​Please feel free to bring a chair or blanket/towel if you’d like to sit inside the bunker to experience the performance. You are welcome to walk around or stand in the space, but there are no seats available in the bunker.
 ​This performance will be recorded and will start promptly at 7pm to ensure that everyone departs prior to the park’s closure at 9pm.
 ​Note that as per park rules, alcoholic beverages or intoxicants of any kind are prohibited.
 ​Jess Tsang is a percussionist, researcher, and improviser dedicated to the creation of new interdisciplinary works. Her sonic practice utilizes bass drums as conduits for tactile feedback loops and acoustic amplifiers for found objects. With a foundation in classical percussion technique, Jess draws inspiration from material culture studies and Foley artists to examine how objects shape our lives, and how that might be translated into music. She released sound shadows, her debut album for amplified bass drum, feedback, and objects, in 2021, and has presented her lecture recital on the intersection of found objects and percussion music at Harvard University.
 ​www.jesstsang.net

Never underestimate the power of connectivity.
 At Harris-Johnson Park, we’re seeing that power in action! The freshly-paved paths at this park do so much more than just improve accessibility. They create seamless, inviting connections between local residents and their shared green spaces.
 When we visited today to capture photos of the finished work, we got to see that impact unfold in real-time: a group of neighbors was already strolling down the new walkways toward the central pavilion for an afternoon game of dominoes. 
 Thoughtfully designed spaces foster real human connection. When we invest in connecting our parks, we invest in connecting our communities.

Historic preservation in America is at a critical crossroads.
 Last week, the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation voted to make significant changes to the federal Section 106 review process, the cornerstone of how the United States considers the impacts of federally funded and permitted projects on historic places.
 Supporters argue the changes will streamline infrastructure and development projects. Critics warn they weaken protections for historic and cultural resources across the country.
 NPR's latest 3-minute story offers a concise overview of what's at stake and why preservation organizations nationwide are 
 Whether you work in preservation, planning, architecture, archaeology, or simply care about the places that tell our nation's story, this is worth a listen.

items.content_text:
What do a local beach and the deep ocean have in common? 
 They both contain plastics. 
 While plastics offer numerous benefits, their proliferation has widespread consequences for both people and the planet.
 In 2020, 435 million tonnes of plastics were produced, and of plastics consumed, almost one-quarter were not safely managed at the end of life. Mismanaged and littered plastics can make their way into oceans. 
 Sustainable plastics production and consumption, together with better waste management, are therefore key to safeguarding ocean health.  
 Learn more via our link in bio ⤴️

Today, we remember former UTC Chancellor Dr. Frederick Obear.
 Serving as chancellor from 1981 to 1997 and later as interim chancellor from 2004 to 2005, Dr. Obear guided UTC through a period of significant growth while remaining deeply committed to student success, academic excellence and the future of the University.
 His leadership expanded academic opportunities, strengthened the institution and helped shape the UTC experience for generations of students. His legacy continues to be reflected across our campus and in the lives of the countless students, faculty, staff and alumni impacted by his service.
 We extend our sincere condolences to the Obear family and all who had the privilege of knowing him. We are grateful for Dr. Obear's enduring leadership, character and service.
 Read more about Dr. Obear's life and legacy: https://blog.utc.edu/…/utc-honors-the-life-and-legacy-of-d…/

 From expanding our Veterans Service Office from one to three officers and opening a satellite location at the Harrison Center, to adding Veterans Day as an official county holiday, fully matching the State’s Property Tax Relief Program to save nearly 4,000 low-income seniors and disabled veterans $2.6 million, and establishing a Veterans Treatment Court, we’re committed to making Hamilton County one of the most veteran-friendly communities in Tennessee.
 Thank you to Post 257 for the invitation and for your continued service to our country and our community. 🇺🇸

 The training covered youth engagement, school security, crisis management, investigations, recognizing signs of child abuse, and mentorship—preparing deputies and officers to serve safely and effectively in our schools. Along with HCSO deputies, officers from the Chattanooga Police Department, East Ridge Police Department, and Marion County Sheriff's Department completed the course and earned their certification.
 Please join us in congratulating these individuals on this achievement! 👏

Where someone lives can determine their employment prospects, career trajectory and overall well-being. 
 The latest edition of the OECD #EmploymentOutlook finds that:
 ➡️ In over half of OECD countries, employment rates vary by more than 20 percentage points across small regions. 
 ➡️On average, the unemployment rate is also more than twice as high in regions with weaker labour markets compared to those with stronger ones. 
 ➡️Exposure to generative AI ranges from around 16% 
 of jobs in some regions to over 70% in others. 
 ➡️Import competition from lower-wage countries risks reducing employment in the manufacturing sector in some countries, with job gains in services only materialising after some time. 
 Overall, people in regions that struggle economically have fewer opportunities to climb the income ladder. 
 Learn more: https://brnw.ch/21x4siD

While students aren't back in the classroom just yet, you may notice more school buses in your community this week. Bus drivers will be conducting test runs to prepare for the first day of school, and buses are already transporting student-athletes to practices and events.

Help keep everyone safe by remembering to:

🛑 Stop for school buses with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm
⚠️ Slow down and stay alert in school zones and neighborhoods
👀 Watch carefully for students getting on, off, or crossing near buses
📵 Eliminate distractions so you can focus on the road

A safe school year starts before the first bell rings. Thank you for helping protect our students, bus drivers, and families! 💛🚌

Pedestrian Struck - Fatality - 5900 block Highway 58
 On July 26, 2026 just before 10:00 p.m., Chattanooga Police responded to a pedestrian struck call in the 5900 block of Highway 58. Upon arrival, officers found a 60-year-old man deceased. 
 CPD's Traffic/DUI Unit responded to conduct the crash investigation. The preliminary investigation determined Vehicle #1 (Acura) was traveling south in the 5900 block of Highway 58 in the right lane of travel. The pedestrian was walking in the roadway in the same lane of travel when the vehicle struck him. The man was pronounced dead at the scene.
 This information is preliminary and is subject to change as the investigation continues. Chattanooga Police ask anyone with information regarding this incident to call 423-698-2525.
 #CPDnews

Shooting – 1100 block Arlington Avenue
 The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) is investigating a shooting that occurred on July 25, 2026 at approximately 6:15 p.m. in the 1100 block of Arlington Avenue.
 Upon arrival, officers located a 19-year-old male  with a gunshot wound. Hamilton County EMS transported him to a local hospital. Meanwhile, a 29-year-old male with a gunshot wound arrived at a hospital via personal vehicle. Both men's injuries were determined to be non-life-threatening. 
 The preliminary investigation determined both men were in the 1100 block of Arlington Avenue and possessed firearms. The exact details are still under investigation and all leads are being followed. 
 CPD Homicide and Crime Scene Units responded to investigate and process the scene. 
 This information is preliminary and subject to change as the investigation continues. Chattanooga Police ask anyone with information regarding this incident to call 423-698-2525.

items.content_text:
Investing in the health, play, and future of students in Hamilton County.
 Through the 2026 Active Outdoor Spaces Grant Program, three local schools are each receiving a $40,000 grant to transform their campuses into vibrant, interactive spaces for outdoor learning and student wellness:
 Hunter Middle School: Cason’s Courtyard, which will feature an inclusive sensory garden and an ADA-accessible playground.
 Calvin Donaldson Elementary: A multipurpose outdoor learning campus designed for active student engagement.
 Big Ridge Elementary: An Outdoor Learning Center pavilion and a community arboretum.
 These three local schools are implementing three innovative projects, all aimed at a shared commitment to fostering healthier, happier students. 
 A special thank you to the Hamilton County Mayor's Office and Hamilton County Schools for their strong partnership and continued investment in our school communities!

 🎓 Voter education for our current election cycle ending on August 6th
 🤝 Relationship building and celebration!

items.content_text:
OECD projections show that New Zealand’s GDP growth is expected to gradually strengthen, reaching 1.4% in 2026 and 2.3% in 2027. However, recent rises in energy prices are likely to slow the pace of growth.
 Higher fuel costs are pushing up inflation in the short term, while increased uncertainty around the global economy and fuel supply is expected to weigh on consumer and business confidence. This could delay spending and investment decisions.
 Overall, while the outlook points to gradually improving growth, careful economic policy management will be needed to keep growth on track.
 Read the #OECD Economic Survey of New Zealand: https://brnw.ch/21x4ptS
 #BetterPoliciesForBetterLives

 Collegedale Airport:

 * ﻿﻿We are working to obtain quotes for an 8ft agricultural mesh wire style fence, to secure the airport perimeter from wildlife. Quotes will include installation and surveyor costs to define the property line on the west side of the airport.

Hamilton County’s Alternative Sentencing Programs team is making a real difference across our community—helping keep our roads, waterways, and neighborhoods clean.
 Community service crews cleaned nearly 58 miles of local roads and highways, collecting 327 bags of litter. They also partnered with Keep Tennessee Rivers Beautiful to collect and recycle more than 60 tires removed from along the river and addressed illegal dumping sites on Lake Resort Drive.
 Thank you to the dedicated officers, supervisors, and participants whose work strengthens our community every day. Residents can also properly dispose of tires at the recycling center next to Silverdale for just $1 per tire.

Last night, our Founding Members gathered at Petal and Pour | Floral Atelier & Café for an exclusive after hours experience inside the beautifully restored Elkins Building.
 One of our favorite parts of being Preserve Chattanooga is creating opportunities for our members to connect with other people who share a love for Chattanooga, historic places, and the stories that make our city special.
 We also love shining a spotlight on local businesses that are breathing new life into historic buildings. Petal and Pour is a wonderful example of how preservation and entrepreneurship can come together to create something truly special.

 Interesting fact: With Lt. Thompson moving to Fire Admin, this marks the first time a member of his family (father and brothers) hasn’t been working on a fire truck since January 1973. Incredible!

Friday, July 24, 2026
 ** ROAD CLOSURE ** 
 The Hamilton County Highway Department is reporting Green Shanty Rd will be closed from July 27, 2026, through August 5, 2026, between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. each day.
 This temporary closure on Green Shanty Rd between Old Lee Highway and Sue Drive is necessary to allow WWTA's contractors to complete repairs to the sewer lines in the area.
 Residents will continue to have access to and from their homes throughout the project.
 All other motorists are asked to avoid the area and allow additional travel time by using the posted detour route. Please refer to the attached map for detour information.
 We appreciate your patience and cooperation as these important infrastructure repairs are completed.
